newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN BEKAERT SEEN BOMBING IN H1 1996.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN BEKAERT SEEN BOMBING IN H1 1996.

text.p: Belgian steel wire and cord maker Bekaert NV will announce late today that current profit plunged around 33 percent in the first half of 1996, but the news will not shock the market, analysts said.
"(The results) will not be very good but I think everyone is prepared for that," Generale Bank analyst Sandra Vandersmissen told Reuters.
"There won't be much impact from the results...we have had enough warning," KB Securities analyst Pascale Weber said.
Both expected Bekaert to post a current result between 30 and 35 percent below 1995's 1.80 billion Belgian francs.
Weber said 1996's first half bottom line profit at about 1.2 billion Belgian francs should be close to the current result.
A 2.2 billion franc capital gain Bekaert made on the sale of shares in Japanese subsidiary Bridgestone Metalpha Corp. will be booked on the second half, she noted.
Vandersmissen forecast current earnings per share at 534 francs, giving a current result also of around 1.20 billion.

BBL analyst Jean-Marie Caucheteux said 1996 earnings per share (EPS), excluding capital gains, would be 1,064 francs, down from 1,414 in 1995. "I have a second half only slightly better than the first half," Caucheteux said.

Analysts said Bekaert's business was squeezed by a slump in demand for steel wire products in the first six months, while forward currency contracts meant the company could not benefit fully from a turnaround in the dollar.
However, most saw a better second half. Vandersmissen forecast full year current EPS at 1,200 francs, more than double her first half figure.
Weber saw a current EPS of 1,135 francs, down from 1,323 in 1995. But with the BMA sale, bottom line EPS would rise to 2,213 francs from 1,340 in 1995, she added.
And analysts did not expect Bekaert shares to suffer unless results came in significantly below expectations or led them to revise their view on the second half of the year.

They noted the shares have already slumped this year from the twin effect of a downgrading in Belgium's Bel-20 Index, due to take place on September 23 but announced in April, and a pre-summer profit warning.
Bekaert, which was already predicting a tough year in March, said in July that it expected full year 1996 current earnings would be 15 percent lower than 1995's 3.0 billion francs.

Bekaert's share ended Tuesday at 23,200 Belgian francs, compared with a year high of 33,000 francs on March 8 and a low of 22,700 on July 16. Since January 1, the Bel-20 index has risen 12.6 percent while Bekaert has lost 4.6 percent.
"Bekaert is being battered by the Bel-20 reshuffle," said Barclays de Zoete Wedd (BZW) Belgium analyst Nicolas de Crombrugghe.
Vandersmissen said Generale Bank was maintaining a sell recommendation on the stock until the reweighting was over.
However, Weber said any move to 22,000 francs should be seen as a buy opportunity. "It's a focused company," she said.
